results.title: Claude Managed Agents Alternatives: 7 Options for 2026
results.content:
Yes. Omnara is an open-source managed agent platform (Apache 2.0) that works with any model, and you can use it hosted or run all of it yourself. Others are partly open source: LangChain's Deep Agents harness (MIT) and the Codex harness behind OpenAI's Agents API (Apache 2.0) are open source, but in both cases the vendor runs the managed part for you.

### Does OpenAI have an equivalent to Claude Managed Agents?

Yes. OpenAI's Agents API, in public beta, runs the Codex harness for you, with sandboxes hosted by OpenAI, by partners, or by you.

### Which alternatives can run Claude models? [...] ### Which alternatives can run Claude models?

AgentCore, LangChain Managed Deep Agents, and Omnara work with any model, including Claude. DigitalOcean Managed Agents offers Claude through its inference platform, and Microsoft Foundry has Claude in its model catalog. OpenAI's Agents API and Gemini Managed Agents only run their own models.

### Can I self-host Claude Managed Agents?

Partly. You can run the sandboxes on your own infrastructure, but Anthropic still runs the orchestration, and tool inputs and outputs still pass through Anthropic. If you need the whole platform on your own infrastructure, you need an open-source platform you run yourself, like Omnara. I compared what each vendor lets you run on your own infrastructure in Self-Hosted Managed Agents. [...] ### LangChain Managed Deep Agents

LangChain's Managed Deep Agents is in public beta. It takes LangChain's open-source Deep Agents harness (MIT licensed) and runs it on LangSmith, with durable execution, sandboxes, and tracing. It works with any model.

It's US-only for now, and it's built around a CLI. You can run the Deep Agents harness yourself anywhere, but not the managed runtime around it. LangChain hasn't published a price for it beyond LangSmith's sandbox rates.

Choose it if you already build with LangChain and LangSmith, plan to stay in that ecosystem, and can work with a US-only beta that has no published price beyond sandbox rates.

results.title: Claude Managed Agents Alternative: 2026 Options Compared
results.content:
TrueForge (MIT, ~6.1k GitHub stars, open-sourced by TrueFoundry in August 2026) is the only one built as a direct substitute: a self-hostable harness that runs the full agent loop with sessions, schedules, sandboxing, approvals, and an HTTP API, on any model provider. Its launch PR claims 50% lower operating costs than Managed Agents; its own benchmark page shows about 30% cheaper on the same model across a small vendor-run test. Treat both numbers as marketing, but the architecture is genuinely the closest drop-in. You supply model keys, a sandbox provider account, and the hosting. [...] There are eight system templates, including Claude Code, OpenClaw, the Hermes agent, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi, and any public Docker image works as a custom template. The `agent37-claude-code` template runs on your own Anthropic account: sign in with `claude auth login`, an OAuth token, or an API key, and model usage bills at exactly Anthropic's rates, with no markup and no middleman. Files, memory, sessions, and connected tools persist until you delete the instance. Scheduled runs, webhooks, public ports, and custom domains are built in, and the whole thing is white-label if you resell agents: you hold the API key, your customers never see us. [...] Claude Managed Agents has been in public beta since April 8, 2026. It is an API product: you define an agent (model, prompt, tools, skills), Anthropic runs it in their own harness and sandbox, and you pay standard Claude API token rates plus $0.08 per session-hour, metered to the millisecond and only while the session is actually running. Idle time is free. Launch customers include Notion, Rakuten, and Asana, and Anthropic now runs its own inbound sales on it.

That $0.08 buys real infrastructure: a production harness, sandboxes, persistent memory stores, multi-agent orchestration, webhooks, scheduled deployments, session budgets with a hard spend cap, and since September 10, the ability to attach your terminal to a live session.

results.content:
‍A: Yes. TrueForge is MIT-licensed and vendor-neutral, running on your own infrastructure with any model. Benchmarked head-to-head on the same 14 enterprise tasks with blind grading, it matched Claude Managed Agents on accuracy at roughly 30% lower cost with the same model, and about 75% lower running an open model instead.

Q: Can I deploy an agent harness in my own VPC or on-prem?

‍A: With an open-source harness, yes - TrueForge runs from a single `npx` command locally, or via Docker Compose and Helm for team deployments with Postgres, Redis, replicas, and OIDC login. TrueFoundry's managed version also runs self-hosted, on-prem, air-gapped, or hybrid, so no data leaves your domain. Claude Managed Agents does not offer this. [...] Before comparing products, it is worth being precise about what you are replacing. Claude Managed Agents is an agent harness - the runtime layer that turns a model into a long-running agent by managing the execution loop, tool calls, context, sandboxing, approvals, and session state. Any replacement has to cover that whole surface, not just the model call.

Five criteria separate real replacements from partial ones: [...] | Feature | TrueForge | Claude Managed Agents | Microsoft Agent Framework + Foundry | deepagents | OpenHands | Pi |
 ---  ---  --- 
| License | MIT / open source | Closed, hosted | Open-source SDK + hosted runtime | Open source | Open source | Open source |
| Model neutrality | Any model | Anthropic only | Any model | Any model | Any model | Any provider, BYOK |
| Benchmark cost / run (Opus 4.8) | $8.50 | $11.80 | — | $21.00 | — | — |
| Cheaper-model option | Yes — $2.90/run with GLM-5.2 | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Self-host / VPC / on-prem | Yes | No | Partial / Azure | Yes | Yes | Yes, local-first |
| Sandbox model | On demand, as a tool | Managed, always-on | VM-isolated per session | Bundled | Docker per session | Local shell |

## Why Open Managed Agents?

Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents is a great product, but it's locked to Anthropic's cloud, Anthropic's models, and Anthropic's access controls. If you work somewhere with a "no data leaves our infrastructure" policy, a multi-provider strategy, a compliance team, or an air-gapped environment, you can't use it at all.

Open Managed Agents ships the same experience — same builder, same templates, same 1:1 API — but runs on your own infrastructure and against any LLM you want.
